title: The household
hookLine: Marcus's hive, Benedict's kitchen rota: whose job is the house?
tomorrow: two travelers walked with a stranger. when did they know him?

lines: NOT GOOD FOR THE SWARM, NOT FOR THE BEE.
cards: A shared apartment has a group chat, and the group chat has a thread about the dishes. A Roman emperor wrote about this, in his way.
In the private notebook we call the Meditations, Marcus Aurelius told himself: "That which is not good for the swarm, neither is it good for the bee."
And a monk named Benedict, writing a rule for a monastery, put the same idea into a kitchen schedule. One question for both: whose job is the house?

teach.h: MADE FOR WORKING TOGETHER, LIKE HANDS.
teach.b: Marcus's answer comes from reason. Elsewhere in the same notebook he says we're made for working together, like feet, like hands, like the upper and lower rows of teeth.
A bee that skips its part isn't getting ahead; it's harming the thing it lives by. Benedict's answer is a rota.

teach.h: NO ONE EXCUSED FROM THE KITCHEN.
teach.b: In his Rule the brothers serve one another in the kitchen, week by week, and no one is excused except for sickness or more urgent work, because, the Rule says, serving earns a greater reward and more charity.
The servers ask the community's prayers as their week begins and ends, and at the end the one finishing washes the towels, and both the outgoing and incoming servers wash everyone's feet.
Here's what the two share: the house isn't a backdrop to the good life. Keeping it is part of the good life. And here's the honest difference.

teach.h: NATURE FOR ONE, PRAYER FOR THE OTHER.
teach.b: Marcus grounds it in nature: we're parts of one whole, so the whole's good is ours.
Benedict grounds it in charity and prayer, under a rule kept together before God. One reasons his way there; the other prays his way there. Each in its own words.

how: Benedictine monasteries share kitchen and house work by rota, as Benedict's Rule directs; readers of Marcus Aurelius take the swarm and the bee as a reason to do their part for the common good.

o: the family you were born into, not the one you chose
a shared home where each part keeps the whole going
a house owned by one person who sets all the rules

games.q: the swarm and the kitchen: tap the pairs.
p: no one excused from the kitchen
wash the towels and everyone's feet

s: Stoicism is about going it alone
Marcus wrote that we're made for working together, like hands and feet.
Benedict excused the sick from kitchen duty
no one was excused except for sickness or more urgent work.
Marcus and Benedict give the same reason for sharing the work
Marcus reasons from nature; Benedict from charity and prayer under a rule.

games.q: in your family the dishes always land on one person. what would Benedict's kitchen do?
o: a rota: everyone serves in turn, week by week, and the turn ends with care.
let the one who minds the mess most handle it; they care the most.
everyone washes only their own dish, so nobody serves anyone.
games.why: in Benedict's Rule the brothers serve one another in turn, and the week ends washing the towels and everyone's feet.

practice: Think of one job in your home that quietly keeps everyone going, the one that's easy to leave for someone else. Decide when you'll take your turn at it, the way Benedict's brothers took their week.
Then sit still with that decision until the bell.

wordCard.voice: The household: a small hive, where the good of the whole and the good of each come to the same thing.

orig.note: Latin: let them serve one another, the opening of Benedict's kitchen chapter.

carryVoice: Carry this: the hive, heard by Marcus in a swarm and by Benedict in a kitchen. Home, first day.

sources.q: That which is not good for the swarm, neither is it good for the bee.

sources.ref: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 2.1 (made for co-operation, like feet, hands, eyelids, the rows of teeth)
Rule of Saint Benedict, chapter 35 (weekly kitchen servers; none excused but for sickness or more useful work; prayers at the start and end of the week; towels and feet washed)
